The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Challenging judgment and award dated 19.07.2017 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- XII,
Ballari, in MVC .no.1414/2016, this appeal is filed by claimants for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- XII,
Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that as result of grievous injuries sustained in an accident that occurred on 23.09.2016, due to rash and negligent driving of APSRTC bus bearing registration no.AP- 15/Z-0066 by its driver, K. Parashuram S/o Durug appa - a pedestrian crossing road, died on spot.
3. Alleg ing loss of dependency, his two wives and four children filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against driver and owner of APSRTC Bus.
4. On contest, wherein claim p etition was opposed on all counts, tribunal framed issues, recorded evidence of claimant no.1 as PW-1 and marked Exhibits - P1 to P11.
In rebuttal, driver was examined as RW-1.

5. On consideration, trib unal held accident occurred due to rash and neg ligent driving of AP SRTC Smt. Thippamma W/O Late K. Prashuram vs Malik Basha S/O Nabi Saheb on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86167112/
2

Bus by its driver and claimants were entitled for compensation of Rs.7,32,500/- as follows:
 Sl. Amount in  Heads  no. Rupees

1 . Loss of dependency 6,07,500/-
 2. Loss of Love and affection and 40,000/-
 moral and financial support.

3. Loss of consortium 50,000/-
 4. Loss of estate 20,000/-
 5. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Total 7,32,500/-
6.
Not satisfied with compensation claimants are in appeal.

7. Sri Manjunath G Patil, learned advocate appearing for claimants sought enhancement of compensation under following heads:
i) Monthly income: On ground that deceased was earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month from real estate and as driver.
But, tribunal consid ered meager income of Rs.7,500/-.
ii) Multiplier: As per Ex.P9 - Driving Licence age of deceased was 54 years attracting multiplier of 11 instead of 9 considered by tribunal.

iii) Future prospects: Tribunal failed to add future prospects as per decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi reported in AIR 2017 SC 2157.
iv) Conventional Heads:

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi reported in AIR 2017 SC 2157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal awarded inadequate comp ensation under conventional heads.
And on above grounds sought for allowing appeal.
8. On other hand, Smt. Aruna R. Deshpande, learned counsel for APSRTC supported award and opposed enhancement.
It was specifically contended that claimants included two wives both of whom could not be treated as dependants either for loss of dependency or while award ing loss of consortium.
Claimants utterly failed to establish monthly income of deceased and on overall consideration, compensation assessed by tribunal was justified .

Smt. Thippamma W/O Late K. Prashuram vs Malik Basha S/O Nabi Saheb on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86167112/
3 9.
From above submission, occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent of APSRTC b us by its driver lead ing to death of K. Parashuram is not in dispute.
Tribunal assessed compensation and held APSRTC liab le to pay same.
APSRTC has not preferred appeal.
Only claimants are in appeal for enhancement.

Thus, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
10.
Insofar as monthly income, though claimants stated that deceased aged 54 years was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from real estate and driving .
Except producing Driving licence, no other specific evidence is led to substantiate same.
Ex.P-9 - Driving Licence of deceased to drive heavy transport vehicle.
Notional income for year 2016 is Rs.8,750/-, which is for ordinary unskilled coolie.
Considering deceased as skilled work man as he possessed Driving licence to drive HTV, his monthly income has to be assessed hig her than coolie.
If it is considered as Rs.12,000/- per month it would be appropriate.
11. Admitted ly deceased was aged 54 years and self employed.
Claim petition is filed by two wives and four children i.e. totally 'six'.

On question whether second wife and her children (illegitimate)
would also be entitled for compensation, this Court in MFA.no.3763/2016 and connected matters disposed of on 14.12.2022, has held even illegitimate children born in live in relationship would be entitled for compensation.
Claims under Motor Vehicles Act, b eing beneficial provisions, meaning of claimants has to extended to 'all dependents'.
There is no serious dispute about b oth wives being 'dependant'.
Thus, both are held to be entitled for compensation.

12. Therefore, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Natio nal Insurance co. Ltd v/s Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in AIR 2017 SC 5127, multip lier applicab le will be 11, addition of future prospects will have to be at '10%' and deduction towards personal expenses will have to be at '1/4'.

entities.text: Natio nal Insurance co. Ltd v/s Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in AIR 2017 SC 5127
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, loss of dependency would be as follows:
Rs.12,000 + 10% -  x 12 x 11 = Rs.13,06,800/-.
13.

Compensation under conventional heads would be as follows:
Each of claimants no.1 and 4 - Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium and each of claimants no.2, 3, 5 and 6 towards parental consortium.
They would also be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and like sum towards loss of estate.

Thus,
total compensation would be:
 Sl. Amount in  Heads  no. Rupees  1. Loss of dependency 13,06,800/-
 2. Loss of consortium 2,40,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- X 6)
 3. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 4. Loss of estate 15,000/-
Smt. Thippamma W/O Late K. Prashuram vs Malik Basha S/O Nabi Saheb on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86167112/
4
Therefore, point for consideration is thus answered partly in affirmative.

14. In result, I pass following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.15,76,800/- as ag ainst Rs.7,32,500/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. APSRTC is d irected to deposit enhanced compensation within eight weeks.
iv. Direction issued by tribunal regarding apportionment and deposit/release shall be as per award of tribunal proportionately to enhanced compensation.

Sd/-
JUDGE GRD Smt. Thippamma W/O Late K. Prashuram vs Malik Basha S/O Nabi Saheb on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86167112/
